Consult Summary:
- Acute onset left arm weakness with accompanying speech difficulties and left facial tingling, concerning for potential stroke; ambulance arranged to transport patient to local hospital for emergency stroke assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Woke up about an hour ago unable to move left arm. Currently, arm cannot move but is not painful. Also reports tingling on the left side of the face and some difficulty with swallowing and speech.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began about one hour prior to the call. Arm weakness and facial tingling persistent since waking; speech difficulty currently noted and described as slower or harder to think through. No change reported since onset besides persistence.
- Associated symptoms: Tingling on the left face; some dysphagia; speech difficulty (slower, more effortful). No arm pain, no numbness elsewhere noted. No discoloration of the hand. No left leg symptoms.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: No specific alleviating factors discussed.
- Other systems: No shortness of breath or chest symptoms reported. No prior similar episodes.
- ROS/negative findings noted: No asymmetry described in facial expression; no eye or limb movements described beyond left arm immobility. Living alone at home during the event. Denied current pain in the arm.
- Relevant negatives: No prior history of similar events. No current left-sided leg symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus type 2.
- Hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin, losartan, amlodipine.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- No other PMH details provided.

Social History:
- Living situation: Living alone.
- Smoking: Former smoker.
- Alcohol: Consumes beer; described as weekend heavy drinking with some during the week.
- Others: Not currently with anyone at home; no other substance use noted.

Family History:
- Father with heart disease (no additional details provided).

Physical Examination:
- Not documented (telephone appointment; no vitals or objective exam findings provided).

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented at this time.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute stroke presenting with left arm weakness, dysarthria/dysphagia, and facial sensory change.
  - Plan:
    - Ambulance to be arranged to transport patient to local hospital A&E for emergency stroke evaluation.
    - Hospital-based stroke team to assess and determine potential treatment.
    - Front door access: patient advised to leave front door unlocked and sit in the hallway to facilitate ambulance arrival; physician will remain on line to monitor and coordinate.
    - Continue line of communication with patient until ambulance arrives.
    - No home management steps beyond ensuring access for emergency services; no medications changes documented.
- General plan: Monitor until EMS arrives; follow hospital stroke protocol upon arrival.

Document Quality:
- Missing elements clinically expected for a consult:
  - Vitals (BP, HR, RR, temp, SpO2) not provided.
  - Neurological exam findings (cranial nerves, motor strength grading, sensory exam, facial droop, gait) not documented.
  - Any imaging or lab results (CT/MNI stroke protocol, glucose, electrolytes) not available.
  - Clear discharge or follow-up plan post-hospital evaluation not defined.
  - Exact medication changes or contraindications not adjusted in clinic.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear, telephone/video-like consult; some conversational pauses, but no evident contradictions.
